Assignment operator should have operands of compatible types
Do not assign function return value to a variable of incompatible type
Do not assign signed constants to unsigned integer variables
Don't treat arrays polymorphically
Declared types of formal and actual parameters to functions must match
Do not cast a signed char to an unsigned int
Incorrect End-Of-String (EOS) definition
Don't assign the dividend of two integers to a floating-point type
Avoid unintentionally discarding the remainder of integer division
Avoid assigning out-of-range value to char type
Avoid assigning out-of-range value to unsigned char type
Avoid overloading class methods on a pointer and a numerical type
Do not create inline non-member functions that contain local static data
Do not slice derived objects
Do not use increment and decrement expressions inside a(b), a[b], and cast
More than one 'enum' type shall not be used as a switch condition or a label in a case statement
Do not call 'sizeof' on constants
Do not call 'sizeof' on a pointer type
Avoid implicit type conversions in assignments involving enum types
Avoid implicit type conversions in comparisons involving enum types
Third parameter to 'memcpy'/'strncpy'/'memmove' should not depend on second
Assignment operators shall not be used in conditions without brackets
The unbounded functions of library <cstring> shall not be used
Narrow and wide string literals shall not be concatenated
String literals with different encoding prefixes shall not be concatenated
String literals with and without encoding prefixes should not be concatenated
A function shall not return a reference or a pointer to a parameter that is passed by reference or const reference
A function shall not return a pointer or a reference to a parameter that is passed by const reference
An object of array type with a specified size should not decay to a pointer when it is passed as a function argument
An object of array type should not decay to a pointer when it is passed as a function argument
An object of array type should not be passed as a variadic argument to a function
An object shall not be assigned to an overlapping object
All constructors of a class should explicitly call a constructor for all of its immediate base classes and all virtual base classes
The execution of a function registered with 'std::atexit()' or 'std::at_quick_exit()' should not exit via an exception
There should be no mismatch between the '%s' and '%c' format specifiers in the format string and their corresponding arguments in the invocation of a string formatting function
There should be no mismatch between the '%f' format specifier in the format string and its corresponding argument in the invocation of a string formatting function
There should be no mismatch between the '%i' and '%d' format specifiers in the string and their corresponding arguments in the invocation of a string formatting function
There should be no mismatch between the '%u' format specifier in the format string and its corresponding argument in the invocation of a string formatting function
There should be no mismatch between the '%p' format specifier in the format string and its corresponding argument in the invocation of a string formatting function
The number of format specifiers in the format string and the number of corresponding arguments in the invocation of a string formatting function should be equal
Pointer arithmetic shall not be applied to pointers that address variables of non-array type
Avoid overloading global functions on a pointer and a numerical type
Avoid overloading namespace functions on a pointer and a numerical type
Avoid implicit conversions from signed to unsigned type
A pointer to an array of derived class objects should not be converted to a base class pointer
Missing comma in a string array initialization
Suspicious argument to malloc
Pointer arithmetic performed on freshly allocated memory
Avoid function calls with incorrect argument order
Function address should not be compared to zero
The values returned by string comparison functions should be compared only to zero
Avoid possible integer overflow in expressions in which the result is assigned to a variable of a wider integer type
Avoid possible integer overflow in expressions in which the result is compared to an expression of a wider integer type
Integer overflow or underflow in constant expression in '+', '-', '*' operator
The same code (after preprocessing) in both branches of if-else statement
An element of an object shall not be initialized more than once
An expression with enum underlying type shall only have values corresponding to the enumerators of the enumeration
Do not copy instances of structures containing a flexible array member
Do not call va_arg with an argument of the incorrect type
The 'abort()' function from the 'stdlib.h' or 'cstdlib' library shall not be used
The 'exit()' function from the 'stdlib.h' or 'cstdlib' library shall not be used
The 'quick_exit()' and '_Exit()' functions from the 'stdlib.h' or 'cstdlib' library shall not be used
The 'terminate' function should not be used
C-style strings shall not be used
Expression statements shall not be explicit calls to constructors of temporary objects only
Use intmax_t or uintmax_t for formatted IO on programmer-defined integer types
Avoid function declarations that are syntactically ambiguous
An initializer using chained designators shall not contain initializers without designators
Integer overflow or underflow in constant expression in '<<' operator
Do not add or subtract a constant with a value greater than one from an iterator
Evaluation of constant unsigned integer expressions should not lead to wrap-around
Evaluation of constant unsigned integer expressions in preprocessor directives should not lead to wraparound
A header file shall not contain definitions of functions or objects that are non-inline and have external linkage
Functions and non-const objects with internal linkage should not be declared in header files
Use multiple include guards
Use unique multiple include guards
An include file should not contain more than one class definition
File with extension '.c' may not include other files with extension '.c'
Never include other files in a file with extension '.icc'
Use multiple include guards with pattern based on the header file name
Use mechanism that prevents multiple inclusion of the file i.e. include guards or "#pragma once" preprocessor directive
"#pragma once" preprocessor directive should not be used in source files
Do not define more than on class in a header file
Every implementation file should declare a local constant string that describes the file
Don't use hard coded value of offset in structures
Don't use hex constant '0xffffffff' as an error marker
A pointer to a long should not be casted to an int pointer
Do not cast an int pointer to a long pointer
Algorithms shall not make assumptions concerning the order of allocation of nonstatic data members separated by an access specifier
The lowercase form of 'L' shall not be used as the first character in a literal suffix
Assigning result of ints operation to long without casting at least one of the ints is not allowed
Do not assign a long int to an int
Do not pass long casted to an int in function call
Do not assign the value from 32 bit multiplication to long type
The type int shall always be declared as unsigned int or signed int
Avoid conversions from "shorter" type to "longer" type in assignment
Do not cast from "shorter" type to "longer" type
Avoid conversions from a "shorter" type to a "longer" type in function calls
Don't use 'i64' or 'L' suffixes directly
Instead of casting a long type operand of an expression to int cast the result of the expression
Do not declare variables of long type directly
Do not assign a long value to a double
The names of identifiers should not be longer than 64 characters
Avoid implicit conversions to a type of narrower size
Avoid implicit conversions of integer constant values leading to data loss
A pointer to a structure should not be passed to a function that writes data to a file
Type long double shall not be used
Type wchar_t shall not be used
User-specified C++ external identifiers should differ in the first 64 characters
User-specified C++ internal identifiers should differ from external identifiers in the first 64 characters
User-specified C++ internal identifiers declared in the same scope should differ in the first 64 characters
User-specified C external identifiers should differ in the first 31 characters
User-specified C internal identifiers should differ from external identifiers in the first 31 characters
User-specified C internal identifiers declared in the same scope should differ in the first 31 characters
The names of identifiers should not be longer than 31 characters
The names of macro identifiers should not be longer than 31 characters
An integer-literal of type long long shall not use a single 'L' or 'l' in any suffix
Do not throw an exception across execution boundaries
Do not pass a nonstandard-layout type object across execution boundaries
Use capital 'L' instead of lowercase 'l' to indicate long
Do not assign int literals to type long
Use arrays of int types instead of large arrays of longs
Use arrays of int types instead of dynamic allocated large arrays of longs
Don't use large arrays of pointers to bool, char, short, int and float types
Don't use macros in include statement
In a macro function, use parentheses before and after multiplication or division
Do not allow absolute or relative path names in #include statements
The #include directive shall use the <filename.h> notation to include header files
Avoid using macro definitions
The #include pre-processor directive will only be used to include header (*.h) files
The #ifndef pre-processor directive will only be used to prevent multiple inclusions of the same header file
The #endif pre-processor directives will only be used to prevent multiple inclusions of the same header file
The #if pre-processor directive will only be used to prevent multiple inclusions of the same header file
The #ifdef, #else, #elif preprocessor directives should not be used
The #if preprocessor directive should not be used
C++ macros shall only be used for include guards, type qualifiers, or storage class specifiers
Macro should not contain token pasting, variable argument list nor recursive macro calls
All macros must expand into complete syntactic units
Pointer dereference operations may not be hidden in macro definitions
A macro parameter immediately following a # operator shall not immediately be followed by a ## operator
The input/output library stdio.h shall not be included
The controlling expression of a #if or #elif preprocessing directive shall evaluate to 0 or 1
Match the filename in a #include directive to the one on the filesystem
#error directive shall not be used
The #pragma directive shall not be used
The '_Pragma' operator should not be used
All macro identifiers in preprocessor directives shall be defined before use, except in #ifdef and #ifndef preprocessor directives and the defined() operator
#undef shall not be used
#undef should only be used for macros defined previously in the same file
The #ifndef, #ifdef, #if, #elif, #else, and #endif pre-processor directives shall only be used for conditional file inclusion and include guards
Do not use the 'bool', 'false' or 'true' identifiers in the #undef directive
Function-like macros shall not be defined
Use angle brackets <> to include standard library headers
Expressions resulting from the expansion of macro parameters shall be appropriately delimited
Don't redefine primitive types
Don't define part of statement
A macro parameter used as an operand to the # or ## operators, which is itself subject to further macro replacement, shall only be used as an operand to these operators
Incorrect 'NULL' definition
Avoid token concatenation that may produce universal character names
The methods inside the SIGNAL and SLOT macros have to exist
Do not force thread termination by calling QThread::terminate()
Do not call new on QMutexLocker
Do not directly set specific Widget attributes that are set by Qt kernel
Every QObject subclass should contain a Q_OBJECT macro
QObject must not be inherited more than one time
It's only possible to connect a signal to a slot or a signal to another signal
Mark signal emissions with the keyword "emit" to distinguish a signal emission from a normal method call
Do not set Idle or Critical priority to QThreads. Use High/Low/Med only
If using lock on a mutex in a function, release the lock in the same function
Declare a copy constructor and operator= for any Qt - inherited objects that have pointers
Never mix const and non-const iterators in assignment
If you use Q_DECLARE_FLAGS, you must also use Q_DECLARE_OPERATORS_FOR_FLAGS
Q_DECLARE_OPERATORS_FOR_FLAGS must be in the global namespace, Q_DECLARE_FLAGS inside the enum's namespace
The getters and setters of a Q_PROPERTY must exist and the types must match
Properties of enum types must use Q_ENUMS
Non-const function should not be called on the Qt object
Do not use setWindowFlags function on a Widget
